diagnostics.message: The binaries-syncer event target can be created in parallel with (or before) aws_lambda_permission.syncer, leaving the schedule rule pointing at a Lambda that events.amazonaws.com is not yet allowed to invoke; the official aws_cloudwatch_event_target docs explicitly require the aws_lambda_permission to be set up for EventBridge to invoke the function. The S3 notification in this same module already handles its equivalent permission with depends_on, but this target does not.

The scale-down event target has no ordering edge to aws_lambda_permission.scale_down; Terraform may register the target on the rule before Lambda allows events.amazonaws.com to invoke, so a rule firing mid-apply would be denied. Per the aws_cloudwatch_event_target docs, the lambda permission must exist for the target to work, and no attribute reference expresses this.

The pool event target depends only on the rule and the pool Lambda, not on aws_lambda_permission.pool; without that ordering, the scheduled target can be attached before events.amazonaws.com is granted invoke permission, causing denied invocations if the schedule fires during apply. The provider docs require the aws_lambda_permission for EventBridge targets to invoke Lambda.

null_resource.update_app registers the webhook URL (api_endpoint + "webhook") with the GitHub App via local-exec, but nothing orders it after aws_apigatewayv2_stage.webhook — the output.webhook chain only reaches the API, Lambda, log group and role, never the $default stage. The script can therefore configure GitHub to call an endpoint that returns 403/404 until the stage is deployed, failing the initial webhook deliveries.
